benchmarks._comment: Benchmark values v2, transcribed from the 2026-08-28 LAUNCH PERFORMANCE OVERVIEW (recomputed panel; quartiles over the historical release panel; Low=P25, Medium=median, High=P75). Cannibalisation 0.2 - the LE standard per the workbook's spend rules (per-release tabs can show 0 via a broken template cell reference; do not transcribe those). See docs/DATA_MODEL.md #4 for provenance and the recomputation policy. Currency GBP.

order_split._meaning: channel share of unadjusted draw+preorder units; renormalise over non-N/A channels at use

spend_rules.cpe_daily_drift_note: Pure time drift in cost per entry, per day, by third of the window. The workbook's 5/7/10% a day (kept in cpe_daily_drift_by_third_workbook) is the cost rise along its own spend path, which ramps 6-10% a day - at spend elasticity 0.38 that ramp alone raises CPE 3.5-5% a day, so applying the tiers on top of the elasticity counted the same effect twice and drove ROI at close under 1 on every campaign. Net of spend, within-campaign drift measures 0.36% a day +/- 1.12 (13 campaigns, 170 campaign-days, etl/analysis/cpe_elasticity.py); 0.5% a day used.

benchmarks.cpe_spend_elasticity_note: Within-campaign elasticity of cost per entry to daily spend, fitted on 13 campaigns / 170 campaign-days with a campaign fixed effect and a day-drift term: 0.384 +/- 0.062 (etl/analysis/cpe_elasticity.py, 2026-09-07). Doubling daily spend raises CPE ~31%, 10x ~2.4x. Set to 0 to price entries flat as before.
benchmarks.cpe_growth_factor_note: Superseded: the forward cost per entry now follows spend_rules.cpe_daily_drift_by_third compounded day by day (the path the ROI chart draws), for the budget and the ROI floor alike. Kept for reference only.
